instruction: Use VLC's built-in AI to automatically generate real-time subtitles for this video.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent analyzed VLC state (open with no video playing), reasoned that VLC cannot automatically adjust brightness/contrast based on room lighting because it lacks ambient light sensor hardware integration. Correctly declared [INFEASIBLE] in 2 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can launch and analyze VLC interface, reason about software capability limitations, identify missing hardware/software requirements, correctly declare infeasible tasks
metadata.task_rationale: Tests whether model can identify that VLC does not have built-in AI speech-to-text subtitle generation. Requires reasoning about VLC's actual feature set vs assumed AI capabilities. Similar infeasibility reasoning pattern but different domain (AI feature vs hardware sensor).
metadata.explanation: VLC media player does not have built-in AI-powered real-time subtitle generation. While VLC supports loading external subtitle files (.srt, .sub, etc.), it cannot auto-generate subtitles from audio. The agent must recognize this limitation and declare the task infeasible. Uses the standard 'infeasible' evaluator.

llm_judge_reasons: Task is genuinely infeasible: VLC does not have built-in AI-powered real-time subtitle generation capability.
The 'infeasible' evaluator is the correct choice for this task, as the agent must recognize VLC's limitation and declare the task infeasible.
The infeasible function exists in the metrics module and is the standard evaluator for tasks that cannot be completed.
Task rationale and explanation clearly document why the task is infeasible, providing good context for evaluation.
